title: Fair-share degradation policy and noise-mitigation orchestrator for Dedicated GPU fleet
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Background: Dedicated customers require throughput guarantees and predictable tail-latency. We repeatedly see transient noisy-neighbor events where a tenant saturates shared resources (SM, PCIe, host CPU) causing other tenants to miss throughput contracts. Existing hard-slicing is too rigid for opportunistic utilization and causes low GPU utilization. Proposal: implement a Fair-Share Degradation Policy (FSDP) and an orchestrator (Noise-Mitigator) that combines continuous noise fingerprinting, preemptible credit buckets, and dynamic soft-quota enforcement to preserve tenant guarantees while improving utilization.

Goals: 1) Ensure P99 latency and committed throughput for reserved tenants under normal load and under neighboring interference; 2) Allow safe transient bursting when spare capacity exists; 3) Reduce evictions and cold restarts by favoring soft degradation paths (quantization fallback, model variant switch, response truncation) before hard preemption.

Scope: runtime + scheduler changes, autoscaler policies, monitoring/observability surface, operator playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: FSDP runs in canary on a subset of Dedicated pools and enforces fair degradation when noisy tenant is detected without causing incorrect evictions.
During 72h stress test with synthetic noisy tenant, reserved tenants maintain >= 95% of committed throughput and p99 latency within SLO for 99% of samples.
Preemptible credit mechanism allows burst exceedance up to credit cap; metrics show credit bucket behavior and correct refill rates documented.
Metrics and dashboards created: per-tenant degradation_score, credit_level, eviction_count, fallback_action_rate; alerts for >3 degraded tenants concurrently.

Automated policy: when degradation_score > threshold, orchestrator triggers a fallback chain (1. reduce max_tokens, 2. swap to quantized variant, 3. redirect to smaller model, 4. hard pause) and logs decisions to audit trail.
Integration tests in CI validate orchestrator decision logic with deterministic inputs; e2e tests validate no regression in Dedicated autoscaling.
design_decisions: Use weighted_degradation_score combining GPU_SM_occupancy_tail, queue_wait_ms, token_throughput_drop, and cache_miss_rate. Weights tuned from historical incidents.
Implement credit buckets per-tenant stored in metadata service with atomic ops; refill_rate linked to reserved_throughput and windowed utilization.
Orchestrator is an independent control-loop service that reads metrics from metrics-api and issues actions via scheduler API (no direct host changes).
Fallback chain prioritized to preserve correctness: prefer model variant/quantization over preemption to avoid warm-start cost.
Expose operator controls: manual override, per-tenant SLO tuning, and debugging flag to force-show noisy fingerprints.
